summary: Off-registry self-named dependency resolves to attacker-controlled URL at install time
details: package.json declares a dependency whose key equals the package's own name (aws-blog) and whose value is the bare HTTPS URL https://repo.securityctrl.com/aws-blog rather than a registry version range. On npm install, npm fetches whatever tarball that host returns and installs it, executing any lifecycle scripts it contains, with no version pin, no integrity hash, and no signature check. The shipped source is an inert stub, so the manifest itself is the entire install-time payload. The name collision with the package's own identifier combined with the implausibly high 45.0.1 version is a dependency-confusion delivery shape intended to win resolution against an internal package of the same name. Whoever controls repo.securityctrl.com controls arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
